request.spec:
The sheet has a policy date (settings, SETTING_CHANGED key=policy-date value=<date>); when it is
blank the policy date is the sheet's today. A claim dated before the policy date rounds half up;
a claim dated on or after it rounds half to even. This decides every rounding of that claim's live
figures (the rate step and the late charge). A correction rounds by the date of the claim it
corrects, not its own. Settled figures stay frozen and figures bound by a statement stay bound.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has a policy date (settings, SETTING_CHANGED key=policy-date value=<date>); when it is
blank the policy date is the sheet's today. A claim dated before the policy date rounds half up;
a claim dated on or after it rounds half to even. This decides every rounding of that claim's live
figures (the rate step and the late charge). A correction rounds by the date of the claim it

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The policy date is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the acceptance spec.

**The rule:** the sheet now has a `policy-date` setting. When it's blank, the sheet's today is used instead. A claim dated before the policy date rounds half up; one dated on or after it rounds half to even. This decides both the rate step and the late charge. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects, not its own. Settled figures and figures bound by a statement are left as they are.

**Server:**
- **Saving the setting:** it accepts a `YYYY-MM-DD` date or blank and refuses anything else. Saving it writes `SETTING_CHANGED ... key=policy-date value=<date>` to the audit file, with an empty value when blank. The settings response now includes `policyDate`.
- **Rounding:** a new `claim/Rounding.java` picks the rounding for each claim. `ClaimFigure` and `Lateness` now take it, and so do everything that calls them: settling, the clerk-limit check, statements, rollups and period totals.

**Front end:**
- **Figures:** the screen works out claim figures itself, so it now follows the same rule. Each claim sent to the screen carries a new `roundsBy` date: its own date, or for a correction the date of the claim it corrects. The screen compares that with the policy date (or today) to choose half up or half to even.
- **Settings form:** it has a new policy-date field (`setting-policy-date`) and shows the current value (`setting-policy-date-current`).

No database migration was needed, because the setting goes into the existing per-sheet settings table.
